content.content: The viewer's renderer shall carry its drawn elements and their measured heights across draws, updating only what a draw changes, and shall absorb a height change's effect on everything below it as a single group translation instead of repositioning, remeasuring or laying out those nodes one by one.
content.rationale: The prerequisite fixes that an interaction's cost follows what that interaction changed and not how many nodes are visible, but names no mechanism by which that relation can hold. This node supplies one, and it has to cover both halves of a draw: the elements the renderer already holds, and the layout movement a change causes. The renderer keeps the elements it has already drawn, and the heights it has already measured for them, between draws, and updates only what a draw changes; carrying each element's identity across draws is what lets a change to one node reach that node and its incident edges only, instead of rebuilding everything on screen, and it is what makes the measured heights of unchanged nodes still usable rather than re-taken. The second half is the one that decides the bound. A change that alters a node's height shifts everything below it, and that shift is not paid per node: the nodes below a change are drawn inside a container that is displaced as a whole, so the entire region below moves by one translation rather than by repositioning, remeasuring or laying out each of its nodes — the region keeps the geometry it already had, and no node inside it is measured, positioned or laid out again. The translation is computed from the height difference the change produced, not from how many nodes happen to sit below the changed node, so it contributes one operation whatever the visible extent below. With both halves in place the work a draw performs is bounded by what the change touched — the changed node, its incident edges, and one displacement of the region below it — and carries no term that grows with the number of visible nodes, which is exactly the prerequisite's condition. It is an elaboration, not a restatement: the prerequisite's sentence contains no renderer, no drawn elements, no measured heights and no displaced region, and this adds the mechanism that makes its cost relation achievable. The licence is the prerequisite's own wording, not an imported rule: it speaks of an interaction being applied to what changed, and this constrains only how a draw computes its result, so nothing outside that relation is decided. It is deliberately restrained: it names no latency or frame budget, no node-count, graph-size or capacity ceiling, and no cache policy that is not tied to what a draw changes. Displacing the region below a height change as one group is adopted only because it is what keeps that part of a draw's work independent of the nodes below, not as a technique chosen for its own sake. It does not contradict the prerequisite: the panel, the interactive HTML page and the interactivity all remain, now with a renderer that keeps its prior output and moves the region below a change as a unit. It is decidable from the recorded statement alone: the refuting observation is a height-changing edit whose work grows with the number of visible nodes below the changed node — positions, layouts or measurements repeated once per node below, or a draw that revisits every visible node — so a reviewer can name the counterexample from the commitment without a rule of their own. The node records the commitment, not any measurement or verdict.
